form_analysis.feedback: Comprehensive spider vein treatment aftercare form with clear differentiation from varicose veins. Well-structured with specific guidance on compression therapy, activity levels, and expected side effects. Good focus on prevention and long-term care. Could be enhanced with more specific timelines for spider vein recovery and procedure-specific details.
form_analysis.note: Form combines general vein treatment information with specific spider vein focus. Some content references multiple treatment types but is adapted for spider veins.

condition_explanation.spider_veins: Spider veins are smaller, superficial veins that can appear red, blue, or purple.
condition_explanation.treatment_options: Common treatments include sclerotherapy, endovenous laser therapy (EVLT), radiofrequency ablation (RFA), and microphlebectomy.

items: Compression: Wear compression stockings or bandages as instructed, usually 24–48 hours continuously, then during the day for up to 2 weeks.
Walking: Begin gentle walking right away; aim for at least 30 minutes daily to promote healing and circulation.
Pain relief: Mild aching, tightness, or bruising is normal. Paracetamol or ibuprofen can help, unless otherwise advised.

activity_guidelines.title: Activity Guidelines
items: Resume most normal activities the same day.
Avoid strenuous exercise, heavy lifting, and high-impact activities for 1 week.
Avoid prolonged standing or sitting – move around every hour.
Avoid saunas, hot baths, and swimming for 1 week after treatment.

wound_skin_care.title: Wound & Skin Care
items: Keep dressings or compression in place as directed.
You may shower after 24–48 hours, but avoid soaking the treated area until fully healed.
Protect the treated skin from direct sunlight for at least 4 weeks to reduce the risk of pigmentation changes.

expected_side_effects.title: Expected Side Effects
items: Mild bruising, redness, or swelling along the vein path.
Temporary firmness or lumps in the treated area.
Itching or tingling sensations.
Slight darkening of the skin over the treated vein (usually temporary).

emergency_guidance.title: When to Seek Medical Advice Immediately
items: Severe pain, swelling, or redness in the leg.
Sudden shortness of breath, chest pain, or coughing blood.
Signs of infection such as warmth, pus, or fever.
Persistent numbness or tingling.

long_term_care.title: Long-Term Care & Prevention
items: Continue wearing compression hosiery as instructed.
Maintain a healthy weight and stay physically active.
Elevate legs when resting to improve circulation.
Avoid prolonged sitting or standing without movement.
